item: An installer or prepare failure after a followed redirect says only a status or a class (R142), and no host list reaches further than its consent-popup lane (R143)
key_paths: src/llm/installer.py; src/safety/fetcher.py; src/ingest/urllib3_log.py; src/ingest/__init__.py; src/wiki/client.py; src/wiki/ores.py; src/services/duckduckgo.py; src/api/llm.py; tests/test_session_host_list.py; tests/test_urllib3_log_withholds_the_path.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md; docs/ledger/RULINGS_INDEX.md
summary: R142: the installer's release lookup and its download answered an HTTP error, a dropped connection, a timeout, an unreadable Location or a body that is not JSON with the exception's own text, which for a followed redirect quotes the signed storage address (query included) into the 500 and the log. Both fetches now raise InstallerFetchFailed (a verification error, so /api/llm/install/prepare answers 502 through http_detail): a fixed sentence per stage plus only HTTP <status> or the exception's class name (src.safety.fetcher.failure_words), raised after the except block so there is no cause and no context, and logged with the same two words and no exc_info. A body that is valid JSON but not an object, or too deep to parse, is the same failure with the class name (TypeError, RecursionError). TransportUnavailable and NetworkBlocked pass through unchanged and a host-list refusal stays InstallerRedirectRefused. The HTTP library's own log lines carried the request target too: urllib3 writes it at WARNING on a malformed header line (a fetch that succeeds) and on a retry, and at DEBUG on the request line and each redirect hop. src/ingest/urllib3_log.py puts a filter on its four loggers (installed by importing src.ingest, so a process that only builds a guarded session has it) that rewrites a target to [path withheld] and keeps an address's scheme, host and port; it never drops a record. Measured on the real library against a loopback socket (a scripted adapter replaces urllib3 and could never show these lines), not assumed: 35 tests, 11 mutants killed, each real-stack case also asserting the library DID log the line. One planted-signature sink test per stage and per kind of failure, each failing only when its own scrub goes (15 mutants killed). R143: a code list is never wider than the consent popup's lane, pinned by one table over 13 lists (POPUP_LANE_LISTS) plus an AST walk that fails on any session built under src/ whose host list is not in the table. WIKI_SESSION_HOSTS is exactly .wikipedia.org, wikimedia.org and stream.wikimedia.org (no .wikimedia.org suffix), ORES_HOSTS is ores.wikimedia.org and the DuckDuckGo ALLOWED_HOSTS is html.duckduckgo.com, each with an exact-list test that only it fails (13 mutants killed). ORES names a refused redirect as its own outcome (refused_redirect) instead of a transport error with the refusal's fixed sentence as the detail (6 mutants killed), because that is the signal Q717's endpoint verification reads. A redirect inside the domain but off the exact host now fails closed with the existing named refusal; whether the real services ever answer that way is an operator look recorded STILL OPEN in OPEN_QUEUE.md (for ORES it is Q717's look too), not an observation. Rows R142 and R143 added to RULINGS_INDEX.
